technical_and_design_decisions: For U1 and U2: Rather than introducing a new internal helper package, inline the small handful of types/methods needed from protoutil, cauthdsl, bccsp, and flogging directly into the consuming package, since the surface area is small and the goal is to eliminate fabric-internal dependencies entirely.

For U1: The statebased package will be reduced to depend only on fabric-protos-go (common, msp, peer) and a minimal local replacement for any protoutil helpers used (e.g., marshaling helpers can be reimplemented in terms of proto.Marshal/Unmarshal or local utilities).

For U2: The entities package will drop bccsp, bccsp/factory, bccsp/sw, bccsp/utils, common/flogging, and common/flogging/fabenc by replacing the few calls with local equivalents (e.g., a simple hash function call and a standard logger).

For U3 and U4: The two stories describe the same fix (adding `tr -d \\` to the base64 export expression) and will be addressed together by updating the tutorial README and the sample script in fabric-samples.

For U5, U6, U7, U8: Externalization will follow the same pattern already used by fabric-protos-go — packages will be moved to a new sibling repository (e.g., fabric-lib-go) with semantic versioning, and both fabric and fabric-sdk-go will be updated to import from the external module.

For U5: protoutil will be split where necessary so that the publicly useful subset (signature marshaling, config block utilities, etc.) lives in the external module while keeping any fabric-internal-only helpers inside fabric.

For U6, U7, U8: The externalized package will be a near-verbatim move of the current code, with the SDK switching from its internal/github.com/hyperledger/fabric/... copy to the new external import path. The SDK's local modifications will be folded into the upstream external package.
Use Go modules with semantic-version tags so downstream consumers (e.g., the Go SDK) can pin to compatible versions and pull in updates via go get.
Maintain backward-compatible Go APIs for all externalized packages; behavioral changes are out of scope.
assumptions: The developer is a senior Go engineer familiar with Hyperledger Fabric internals, the fabric-protos-go externalization pattern, and the Fabric Go SDK build.
A new repository (fabric-lib-go) is assumed to exist or will be created with proper CI, license, and contribution guidelines mirroring fabric-protos-go.
The Fabric Go SDK is the only downstream consumer that needs to be updated when packages are externalized; any other downstream consumers are not in scope for this increment.
U3 and U4 are duplicate reports of the same tutorial issue and are addressed as a single activity.
All existing unit and integration tests must continue to pass after each change; no new feature work is included.
Code review, PR submission, and CI infrastructure are available — effort for those is included in the cross-cutting integration activity.

Crypto and signing helpers needed by the statebased and entities packages can be reimplemented locally with stdlib + protos without sacrificing correctness, as the methods used are small and well-defined.
The externalized BCCSP, MSP, and discovery-client packages will not require re-licensing; existing Apache-2.0 license headers carry over.
